record.context_brief: Maximal symmetry numbers in higher-dimensional Euclidean space
record.original_question: Let X be a compact subset of R^n with positive Lebesgue measure, where n > 2, and let ms_r(X) denote the largest measure that is guaranteed for a monochromatic symmetric subset in every measurable r-coloring of X. Classify the numbers ms_r(X) for such sets X. In particular, determine ms_r(X) for every regular convex polyhedron in R^n with n > 2, and determine ms_2(T) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3.

evidence.quote: For such a triple X = (X, µ, S) (called a symmetry measure space) we shall evaluate the maximal symmetry numbers msr(X) equal to the maximal measure of a symmetric subset that can be found in each measurable r-coloring of X.

Problem 5.4. Classify maximal symmetry numbers msr(X) of compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in Rn for n > 2. In particular, calculate msr(X) for all regular convex polyhedra X in Rn for n > 2. Calculate ms2(T ) (or equivalently, ms2(S4 × I)) for the regular tetrahedron T in R3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n > 2 and let X ⊂ ℝⁿ be a compact set of positive Lebesgue measure. A subset A ⊂ X is called symmetric if there exists an isometry s: ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ of order 2 (i.e. s ≠ id and s∘s = id, so s is a reflection through some affine subspace, or a point/central symmetry, or a composition giving an involution) such that s(A) = A and s preserves X (s(X) = X). Given a positive integer r, a measurable r-coloring of X is a partition X = C₁ ∪ … ∪ Cᵣ into Lebesgue-measurable pieces. Define the maximal symmetry number 
   msᵣ(X) = inf_{χ} sup { λ(A) : A ⊂ Cᵢ for some i, A symmetric, A measurable },
where the infimum runs over all measurable r-colorings χ of X and λ denotes n-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

(a) Classify, as completely as possible, the values msᵣ(X) over all compact subsets X ⊂ ℝⁿ of positive Lebesgue measure for n > 2 and all integers r ≥ 2.

(b) For every regular convex polyhedron X ⊂ ℝⁿ with n > 2 (i.e. each regular polytope: simplex, cross-polytope, hypercube, and the additional regular polytopes in dimensions 3 and 4), compute msᵣ(X) for all r ≥ 2.

(c) For the regular tetrahedron T ⊂ ℝ³, determine the exact value of ms₂(T).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed by Banakh and collaborators in work on Ramsey-type symmetry numbers. Exact values of msᵣ are known only in restricted settings (segments, regular polygons in the plane, figures of revolution, multidimensional parallelepipeds). No source located computes ms₂(T) for the regular 3-simplex or completes the classification for higher-dimensional regular polytopes, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Exact values of ms_r have been determined for figures of revolution, regular polygons, and multi-dimensional parallelepipeds; higher-dimensional regular polytopes are not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classifications of msᵣ(X) are available; the regular tetrahedron and other higher-dimensional regular polytopes are not resolved there.

status_evidence.title: Symmetric monochromatic subsets in colorings of the Lobachevsky plane
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent works extend the symmetry-number framework to other geometries but do not compute ms_r for regular polyhedra in R^n, n>2.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up literature does not solve the classification or the ms₂(T) computation for the regular tetrahedron.
